nodes.name: Create Lead

parameters.query:
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
biz AS (
  SELECT b.business_id FROM vaibhavcapstone_businesses b, p
  WHERE b.business_id = p.j->>'business_id'
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_leads
    (lead_id, business_id, trace_id, channel, from_email, subject, body, raw_payload, received_at, status)
  SELECT p.j->>'lead_id', biz.business_id, p.j->>'trace_id', p.j->>'channel',
         p.j->>'from_email', p.j->>'subject', p.j->>'body_text', p.j->'raw',
         COALESCE((p.j->>'received_at')::timestamptz, now()), 'RECEIVED'
  FROM p, biz
  RETURNING lead_id, business_id, trace_id
),
evt AS (
  INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_events (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, agent, action, actor, detail)
  SELECT business_id, lead_id, trace_id, 'intake', 'LEAD_RECEIVED', 'system',
         jsonb_build_object('channel', (SELECT j->>'channel' FROM p))
  FROM ins
  RETURNING event_id
)
SELECT ins.lead_id, ins.trace_id, ins.business_id, 'RECEIVED' AS status FROM ins;

parameters.content:
## The front door

Every enquiry enters the system here, whatever it came from — an ordinary email, a chat message from the business's own staff, or another company's AI agent. They all arrive at this one address, in the same shape.

That's deliberate: **nothing downstream ever needs to know how a customer reached us.**

### Check what arrived

**One address; anything may knock.**

**Does it make sense?** Is there a business, a sender's address, and some actual text? Is the address even shaped like an address?

We also stamp two identifiers here: one naming this enquiry, and one for tracking it across every step that follows. That second one is what lets you follow a single enquiry through the whole system later.

### Write it down before anything else

**The enquiry is recorded immediately** — before any AI, any decision, any judgement. If everything after this point fell over, the enquiry would still be safely written down.

**If the request was malformed**, the rejection itself is recorded and we answer with a clear "that wasn't valid". Even a bad request leaves a trace; nothing is silently dropped.

### Answer fast, then do the work

**Answer straight away — "received".** Whoever sent it doesn't wait while we think; the acknowledgement goes back in a fraction of a second. The real work happens after.

**Don't recognise the business?** Recorded, and answered honestly with "we don't know that business" rather than quietly swallowing the enquiry.

**Then hand on the job ticket** to the workflow that reads the email. Everything from here on works from this one record.

## Why one door matters

Email, chat and other companies' AI agents all funnel into this same address.

Adding a new way for enquiries to arrive means writing a small adapter that knocks on this door — not touching the pipeline behind it. That's exactly how the agent-to-agent door was added late in the build without disturbing anything that already worked.

## Known limitation, stated honestly

**This door isn't password-protected.** Anyone who knows the address could post an enquiry to it.

That's acceptable for a local demo and it's the first thing to fix for real use: a key per business, checked here. It's listed as the biggest known gap in the write-up rather than quietly left out.
